trigger: Meta Ray-Ban Gen 3 dominates with 94% display-less market share; AI glasses shipments surge 263% YoY in H1 2026 (Counterpoint Research). Google, Samsung, and Snap entering late 2026 signal platform phase beginning.

timeline.event: Meta & EssilorLuxottica launch Ray-Ban Stories — first camera-equipped fashion AI glasses, seeding the consumer category
Meta Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 2) ships with Meta AI voice assistant, multimodal camera; first AI-native glasses at consumer scale
AI glasses shipments hit 1M+ units in a single year (210% YoY growth, Counterpoint); Baidu, RealWear, and Vuzix enter enterprise segment
Meta Ray-Ban Display launches with integrated HiRes lens screen + Neural Band wrist controller; EssilorLuxottica reports 7M AI glasses sold in 2025
Google announces Warby Parker + Gentle Monster Android XR partnership; Alibaba launches Quark AI glasses; Meta acquires 3% stake in EssilorLuxottica
AI glasses shipments surge 263% YoY (Counterpoint); Meta holds 94% of display-less segment; Samsung Intelligent Eyewear announced July 2026; Apple delays to late 2027

pestal.impact: EU regulators drafting enforcement policy on smart glasses surveillance; CNIL (France) issued warning + action plan May 2026; Norway and Germany governments initiating stakeholder reviews and legal complaints

Wearable AI market at $69.8B in 2026 (Meticulous Research) growing at 14.5% CAGR to $270B by 2036; Meta + EssilorLuxottica partnership generating €3B+ hardware revenue; $212B AI VC funding in 2025 accelerating wearable investment

Smartphone fatigue and screen-time anxiety driving hands-free tech adoption; Gen Z and Millennials normalizing glasses-as-interface; creator economy demanding first-person POV content; simultaneous backlash against bystander surveillance

On-device AI (Snapdragon AR1 Gen 2, Meta custom chip) enables multimodal glasses without cloud lag; open-ear speaker tech matures for daily wear; 4-hour battery now viable for commute use; Gemini + GPT-4o enable contextual vision AI in real-time

300M+ eyewear frames replaced globally per year creating circular-economy opportunity for AI lens retrofitting; accelerating upgrade cycles risk increased e-waste without manufacturer take-back programs

GDPR applies to bystander data captured by AI glasses; EU AI Act Article 50 (transparency obligations) effective August 2026; EPIC urging FTC to block Meta's 'Name Tag' facial recognition feature; CNIL warns French Penal Code Article 226-1 may apply (1yr prison, €45K fine)

competitors.name: Meta Ray-Ban (Gen 3 + Display)
competitors.detail: Undisputed category leader. Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 at $449, Display at $799. 94% display-less share in H1 2026. AI assistant, 12MP camera, 4h battery. 7M units sold in 2025 via EssilorLuxottica. Gen 3 adds multi-frame styles and neural gesture control.

competitors.name: Google Android XR Glasses
competitors.detail: Late 2026 launch. Gemini-powered, Android XR OS. Partners: Warby Parker (fashion-forward) + Gentle Monster (designer). Target: 2M units in 2026 launch window. Pricing undisclosed. Strong app ecosystem advantage over Meta's closed platform.

competitors.name: Samsung Intelligent Eyewear
competitors.detail: Announced July 22, 2026. Galaxy AI integration with Bixby + Gemini. Samsung Galaxy Ring synergy for health data. Pricing TBD. Targets Galaxy phone users as natural upgrade path. Hardware designed with Gentle Monster — direct style competition to Ray-Ban.

competitors.name: Rokid Max / Rokid AR Studio
competitors.detail: China-based AR display leader with 41% of display-glasses segment. Enterprise focus: field service, remote assist, training. Qualcomm Snapdragon XR2+ chipset. B2B pricing $599–$1,299. Growing US and EU presence through enterprise channel.

competitors.name: Snap Spectacles (Gen 5 AR)
competitors.detail: Creator-focused waveguide AR glasses. Limited commercial availability. Positioned for social-native use cases and developer/creator community. Niche but influential for setting UI/UX expectations for AR overlays in fashion + entertainment contexts.

canvas.who: Urban Millennials and Gen Z professionals (25–38) in developed markets; fashion-conscious; daily smartphone-dependent; open to AI-enhanced accessories; early adopters who already wear eyeglasses or sunglasses
canvas.where: City commutes, international travel, gyms and outdoor runs, open-plan offices, concerts and live events, retail environments — anywhere hands-free access beats phone-out interactions
canvas.why_now: Three forces converging in 2026: (1) on-device AI is finally small enough to live in a glasses frame without cloud dependency; (2) Meta proved the form factor works at 7M units/year, removing consumer hesitation; (3) Google + Samsung entering signals platform maturity — the 'app store for glasses' moment is arriving
canvas.behavior: Wearing AI glasses as default eyewear for outdoor use; using voice-first AI queries instead of unlocking phone; posting first-person POV clips on Instagram/TikTok as a differentiator; replacing earbuds with open-ear glasses speakers for awareness + audio
canvas.unmet: Prescription lens compatibility at accessible price; battery life beyond 4 hours for full-day use; truly discreet camera (no blinking LED) that respects privacy norms; platform openness (Meta's walled garden frustrates developers); waterproof rating for all-weather use

takeaways: Creators: Build first-person POV content series using AI glasses — the glasses-cam perspective is authentic, novel, and highly shareable. Meta's camera quality has reached 'good enough for Reels' and the format is still wide open.

Builders: Target prescription glasses users (43% of adults) — the entire category is dominated by non-prescription sunglasses. A brand that solves daily prescription AI glasses at sub-$300 captures a market no one owns yet.

Investors: Watch the Google/Samsung Android XR ecosystem — it could commoditize AI glasses hardware the way Android commoditized smartphones, compressing Meta's margins and opening a long tail of OEM opportunities.

Developers: Meta's platform API is open now, and the AI glasses app store is essentially empty. Build voice-first, contextual, camera-aware apps today — the distribution advantage of early mover status will be significant when Google/Samsung open their stores later in 2026.
